The Airport Police Command says it has established contact with the family of Abraham Safety Osakpolor, a Nigerian-Canadian who died after being hit by a vehicle along the Murtala Muhammed International Airport access road in Lagos. The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, following an earlier appeal for members of the public to help locate the deceased’s relatives. “The Command wishes to inform the general public that following its earlier press release seeking assistance in identifying the family and friends of late Abraham Safety Osakpolor, contact has now been successfully established with his family,” the statement said. The command expressed appreciation to individuals, media organisations and members of the public who shared its earlier announcement, saying their cooperation helped achieve the outcome. It quoted the Commissioner of Police, Airport Police Command, CP Olufunke Ogunbode, as reiterating the command’s commitment to maintaining a cordial relationship with the public. PUNCH Online reported that the 58-year-old, who was born in Benin City, Edo State, was hit by a moving vehicle while walking along the expressway leading from the airport towards the Oshodi axis. He was rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead, while his remains were deposited in a morgue. The police also said the motorist involved in the accident was apprehended and would be charged in court. During an initial search, officers recovered a Nigerian passport and a mobile phone without a SIM card from his belongings. A Canadian passport was later discovered by mortuary attendants.
